title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

sense.text: “Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God”. Everything happens because the Lord allows it. There is a power behind what your eyes see; what you see is not always what it is. Remember the servant whose eyes had to be opened to see the army with the prophet. In these latter days, do not lean on your own understanding, speak foolishly, or lose faith because you cannot see what God is doing. Put your trust in God and stay upon this faith. The Lord can be doing something greater than the thing you are looking at.

“For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child”. These global problems are contractions. A woman has a contraction, then a pause, then another; the contractions get closer together, from five minutes to four, three, two, one, until the baby comes. Likewise trouble comes, slows down, and makes people think everything is all right, then another trouble hits. The Lord makes his entrance at the end of those contractions, like a thief in the night.

Do not sleep on what is happening. The pandemic is an experiment to see how society reacts; people are buying guns and running out of ammunition. It is only the beginning. A peace agreement between America and Iran does not mean safety, and China is not the next world ruler. After Esau comes Israel; that is our time to rule. Keep faith through the lulls as well as the trouble.

“Moreover I freely set at liberty every one of the Jews, that were carried captives out of the land of Judea into any part of my kingdom”. Our people were scattered throughout that kingdom, including Asia Minor. Diaspora means scattered. The seven churches were established among these Israelite colonies; do not look at their Greek place names and imagine that the letters were addressed to all races.

The history of the northern diaspora describes the Seleucids taking Judea and Antiochus III moving thousands of Jewish soldiers and their families into Asia Minor. Antiochus III is the ruler in that account, not Antiochus Epiphanes. Taking the Apocrypha out hides this history from people reading the New Testament. The suffix in Jewish is being used for people who are something like the originals, converts, just as five-ish is not exactly five o'clock. Keep the original Israelites and converts distinct.

John was exiled on the island of Patmos. Look at its location in relation to Asia Minor: the seven churches were in that region of the Greek empire, where our people had been scattered. Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira and the other churches were Israelite congregations in those settlements. That history and geography come before reading the messages to their leaders.

“Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write”. The angel is the leader of the church, a man entrusted with the congregation. This is not a letter addressed to Michael, Gabriel or another heavenly angel. Christ holds the seven stars and walks among the seven golden candlesticks: the stars are the leaders and the candlesticks are the seven churches, like the seven-branched menorah.

Christ knows their works, labour and patience. They cannot bear evil and have tested men claiming to be apostles, finding them liars. All of the apostles were not true apostles. There were men pretending to have walked with Christ and received his teaching, then setting themselves up over the churches. That same spirit appears when inexperienced brothers want authority before they have learned. You cannot compare somebody's two chapters to another man's thirty chapters and act as though you are on the same level.

“And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name’s sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.” They carried this truth, endured and kept working for Christ without giving up. These are good works, and Christ acknowledges them before correcting what is wrong.

“because thou hast left thy first love”. The first love is Christ. A congregation can have patience, labour and the ability to expose false teachers and still need this correction. Loving Christ cannot be separated from loving the brothers he has put before you. God first showed his love by sending his Son; that obligates us to love one another.

precepts.why: “thou art good in my sight, as an angel of God”. Achish is speaking to David, a man. Angel can mean a human messenger. That is how the angel addressed in Ephesus is the man leading that church, not one of the heavenly angels.

“The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.” Revelation gives its own explanation. The stars in Christ's right hand are the leaders; the seven golden candlesticks are their congregations. Christ is walking in the midst of those churches.

Paul cuts off the occasion sought by men who want to glory as though they have the same standing as the apostles. “For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.” They were pretending to be men Christ had taught, pretending to have walked with him. The false apostles were inside the church, not merely enemies outside it.

“for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” Satan did not approach Eve as a snake crawling on its belly; he came appearing righteous. Likewise his ministers transform themselves into ministers of righteousness, though their end is according to their works. Men can be among the congregation, look righteous and still be ministers of Satan, disrespecting Paul, Peter, James and John.

“Let no man think me a fool”. Paul is not stupid. If they insist on treating him like a fool, receive him as a fool while he boasts a little and gives his credentials. He has to establish what he has actually done because deceitful men are trying to put themselves on the same level. That is the kind of claim Ephesus tested and found to be a lie.

God manifested his love by sending his only begotten Son so that we might live through him. Christ is the first creation, the Alpha and Omega, and the propitiation, the mediator for our sins. We did not love God first; he loved us and sent his Son. If God so loved us, we ought to love one another.

“We love him, because he first loved us.”. Then John puts that love to the test: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar”. How are you going to love God, whom you have not seen, while hating your brother, whom you have seen? Claiming to love Christ while rejecting the brothers is hypocrisy. That is how to examine whether you have left your first love.

sense.text: “that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you”. The requirement is one mind and one judgment. Paul heard from the household of Chloe that there were contentions among them. Unity is the correction; picking a faction is the problem.

Some said they were of Paul, some Apollos, some Cephas, and some Christ. All four parties were wrong. Saying that you only follow Christ sounds righteous, but in that contention it was another division. “Is Christ divided?” No. Paul was not crucified for them and they were not baptized in Paul's name.

Christ was not physically on the earth while Paul was writing to this church. A man saying he follows only Christ can use that claim to reject every man Christ appointed to guide him and then do whatever he wants. God has always used men. You learned that you were an Israelite through somebody; you did not teach yourself everything. Do not claim an angel taught you while denying the men whose classes you actually learned from. The people who demanded to hear God instead of Moses were frightened when they heard his voice and wanted Moses to speak again.

precepts.why: “for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” You have seen the brothers Christ uses, but you have not seen Christ. Rejecting all those brothers while claiming you only love Christ does not fulfill this command. It is the same problem as claiming Christ as a faction against the men he sent.

Philip heard the eunuch reading Esaias and asked whether he understood. “How can I, except some man should guide me?” The eunuch asked Philip to sit with him. He needed a man to guide him in the scriptures. Having a Bible in your hand does not remove the need for teachers appointed by God. That is why the party claiming only Christ was wrong along with the other factions.

sense.text:
Remember where you fell, repent and do the first works. Go back to the zeal you had when you first heard the truth, when you wanted to study and do the work. Examine yourself instead of making everybody else prove what is wrong with you. Your works speak. Somebody can appear to be a good brother and still cheat on a test; what you allow others to see is not the whole of your spirit.

Worldly cares, money and lust can choke the word. Brothers in Austin let money problems overthrow them and would not repent. Being removed and then saying that you are still in the truth, without correcting the sin, is not repentance. Get back to your first works; if opening the Bible now only makes you fall asleep, recognize that change.

“or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.” The candlestick is the church and its light is the law and understanding. Christ can take that understanding away. Whatever little truth you still have can be removed if you will not repent.

The Nicolaitans were Israelites worshipping Nike, the Greek goddess of victory. Christ hates those deeds. He does not accept every form of worship simply because an Israelite practices it. Ephesus was right to hate what he hates.

Hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The promise to the one who overcomes is to eat of the tree of life in the paradise of God. Eating is learning the doctrine of life, the knowledge of God's commandments. The fruit is immortality, living and ruling for ever. Do not reduce the tree to Eve eating an apple; understand what that eating represents.

precepts.why: “Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way”. Kiss means love the Son, Christ, and keep his commandments. His wrath can kindle only a little and you perish. Blessed are those who trust in him. Leaving your first love is serious; return to that love through obedience, not words alone.

“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” Find where you went wrong and correct it. Do not make this everybody else's responsibility. Christ is in you unless you are reprobates, void of judgment. Look at your works and examine what only you and the Lord know, not just the appearance you have before the brothers.

The seed among thorns is people who hear the word, but the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things enter and choke it, leaving it unfruitful. Money and sex are two great stumbling blocks. You can have heard and received the truth and then let these things destroy it. That is how somebody who once had zeal needs to return to the first works.

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The candlestick carries the light of God's law. Refusing the reproof that leads to life brings the threat of losing that light. Christ is not talking about merely moving furniture; the church can lose its understanding.

“unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.” Those who have understanding receive more. If you let it go, even the little you still have is taken away. That is what removing the candlestick means.

“The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”. Knowledge of the commandments is the doctrine of life. The people who do what pleases God receive the fruit of that tree, immortality. Eating the tree of life means receiving and doing this doctrine, not eating a literal apple.

sense.text: The angel of Smyrna is its leader, just as the angel of Ephesus is a man. The first and the last, who was dead and is alive, is Christ. Smyrna, Ephesus and Pergamos competed for the standing of chief city in Asia Minor. Smyrna became a bishopric, a church under a bishop, growing from the Jewish colony there. Keep that Israelite history in mind.

Christ knows their works, tribulation and poverty. They are poor under Roman oppression but rich in the promises given to Israel. He also knows the blasphemy of people who say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

Do not confuse that with every time Christ rebuked actual Jews. In John 8 he explicitly acknowledged Abraham's seed while condemning their conduct. The issue here is people claiming the identity who are not the original people. Herod and his descendants were Idumaean converts installed in authority, and the same robbery of our name, heritage and land continues. When somebody claims the modern state fulfills Israel's restoration, read every condition of the prophecies.

precepts.why: “but received me as an angel of God”. Paul is a man, and the Galatians received him as God's messenger. That is another example of angel describing a human leader, explaining the angel of the church in Smyrna.

“his bishoprick let another take.” Judas held an office among the apostles; after his death another was to take that office. Bishopric is the office and charge over the church. The history calling Smyrna a bishopric is describing that church organization.

Christ addressed Jews, and they answered that they were Abraham's seed and had never been in bondage to any man. Christ answered, “I know that ye are Abraham’s seed”. He knew their lineage; he was not saying that these people were impostors with a false genealogy.

When he said “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do”, he was speaking of their deeds and the Roman influence they followed. Their conduct came from the devil even though their flesh came from Abraham. Do not use Cain, who was before the flood, as though he were Esau, who came after it. Keep the people and the times straight. Revelation 2:9 addresses a different claim: people who say they are Jews and are not.

“also the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision; but they shall fall.” The king of the south is Ptolemy. The robbers of our people steal our heritage, land and name, then exalt themselves as though the visions belong to them. They can set themselves up, but the prophecy says they will fall.

“There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea”. Being called king of Judaea does not make Herod an original Israelite. The dictionary identifies the Herods as Idumaean rulers of Palestine. Idumaea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. Rome installed a converted Edomite family as kings over our people.

Paul is glad to answer before Agrippa because he is expert in the customs and questions among the Jews. Agrippa belongs to that Herodian family. Their conversion and circumcision made them knowledgeable about Jewish customs; knowledge of those customs does not change their lineage. This is how a ruler can be familiar with Israel's religion without being an original Israelite.

The Lord speaks against the residue of the heathen and all Idumea, “which have appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds, to cast it out for a prey.” Idumea is Edom. The land being taken into possession in 1948 does not prove those people are Israel; the prophecy describes Idumea taking God's land, with other nations sharing in the matter.

sense.text:
The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, choose Israel again and set them in their own land. Strangers will be joined to the house of Jacob. “and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” The nations that held Israel captive become Israel's servants and handmaids. That is a condition of the promised return, not something to skip while pointing at a modern state.

If those in the land today fulfilled this return, where are the nations that enslaved them now serving them? You cannot take only the words about returning and ignore the reversal of captivity and rule. The descendants of the people enslaved throughout the Americas have not yet received that promise.

The Lord gives Israel rest from sorrow, fear and the hard bondage in which they were made to serve. Our bondage was centuries long, with enslavement, abuse and loss of our identity. The Holocaust comparison in the video does not establish this promised rest for our people. Read the conditions God gave instead of accepting the preacher's identification of Israel.

The vision concerns Judah and Jerusalem in the last days. The mountain of the Lord's house is the government of the kingdom, established above the other governments. All nations flowing to it is our people coming from the nations where they were scattered. They come to learn God's ways and walk in his paths; the law goes forth from Zion and the word from Jerusalem.

Look at the present land and ask whether that government is teaching God's law. The conflicts, the pork and the parades do not match that kingdom. Do not announce fulfillment simply because a country has been given the name Israel.

“they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”. Nation does not lift up sword against nation and they do not learn war any more. That is world peace under the kingdom, not continuing warfare and conflict in the land. The modern situation fails the conditions of the prophecy being used to identify it.

precepts.why: God gathers the nations into the valley of Jehoshaphat to plead with them for “my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” Israel was scattered and the land divided. The dispute over the land between Palestinians and those called Jewish does not mean the restoration has been completed. God still has a controversy over what the nations did to his people and his land.

sense.text:
“for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.” God confirmed the evil he spoke against us and our judges. The curses beginning at Deuteronomy 28:15 and continuing through verse 68 describe the calamities upon our people: enslavement, removal, rape, mutilation, the destruction of families and the loss of language, nationality and heritage. The twelve tribes are the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native American Indians. There is no nation on earth whose atrocities can be equaled to what happened to them. You cannot compare a five-year Holocaust to what happened to us.

The captivity runs from the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70 through dispersal into Africa, the era of 1492, the Atlantic trade and the plantations, including the Middle Passage and slavery throughout North and South America. It is not just one country or one short period. Whole generations were stripped of their identity. Two hundred million died in the Middle Passage and over 200 million from North to South America. The Nigerian man who claimed that the Jewish people suffered worse in those five years was repeating powerful brainwashing, and the audience rejected it.

The oppression also continues through debt and control of nations: Haiti was made to pay France for its freedom, Aristide demanded the money back, and African countries are told to keep their money in French banks, where France invests it, then to borrow a small amount back while vastly more is taken from their resources. Children have no shoes while that wealth is removed. Haiti is charged for the money France lost by no longer having them as slaves. If you do not know what evil is, think about that: that is the white man being the devil. When Guinea demanded independence in 1958, France destroyed what it could rather than simply leave the country free. These are parts of the breach that only Christ can heal.

precepts.why: “for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?” What people can be compared to Jerusalem in order to comfort her? Our breach is as great as the sea. The centuries of captivity, destroyed families, loss of names and language, and continuing exploitation cannot be healed by those who inflicted them. Only Christ can heal that breach. This explains the evil Daniel says has not been done to another people under the whole heaven.

sense.text: The people have been brought back from the sword, gathered from many peoples into mountains that were waste, and dwell safely. That is the setting for Gog and Magog. It is not the present state being attacked while it remains in conflict; read when this gathering and safety take place.

“I will go up to the land of unwalled villages”. These people are at rest and dwell safely without walls, bars or gates. That description does not fit present Jerusalem. Revelation places the attack after the thousand years, when Satan is released and the nations surround the saints and the beloved city.

precepts.why:
After the thousand years are expired, Satan is loosed out of prison. He goes out to deceive the nations in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, and gathers them in a number like the sand of the sea. They surround the camp of the saints and the beloved city, and fire comes down from God out of heaven to devour them.

That is the timing of Ezekiel 38. The white man is released after the thousand years, gathers the nations against the kingdom, and God destroys that assault. Applying Gog and Magog to the people currently occupying the land overlooks both the thousand years and the condition of the restored people dwelling safely.

sense.text: The ones who say they are Jews and are not are the synagogue of Satan. The history of Edomite rulers and the unfulfilled conditions of Israel's return expose that false claim. Smyrna's material poverty does not remove the riches of God's promises to the true Israelites.

Fear none of the things you will suffer. The devil casts some into prison so they may be tried, just as Herod imprisoned the apostles under Rome. Ten days is the period of tribulation appointed to them. Christ commands faithfulness unto death and promises a crown of life. Some of us may have to die for the truth; that death is precious to the Lord.

The one who overcomes will not be hurt by the second death. That is the lake of fire, not ordinary death. The first resurrection is at Christ's coming; the elect have already been judged and the second death has no power over them. The rest of the dead come afterward, when the thousand years are finished.

Do not assume that being your mother or father makes somebody exempt. Family members who died without believing will face that judgment. Burning a body or scattering ashes in the sea does not prevent resurrection. God brings the dead back from wherever they are and judges every man according to his works.

precepts.why: Herod stretched out his hands against the church, killed James the brother of John with the sword, and then took Peter because killing James pleased the Jews. Peter was apprehended and put in prison. Herod is the Edomite ruler under Rome. That history shows the devil casting believers into prison and trying them; the warning to Smyrna is something the church had already experienced.

“Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.”. If you remain faithful and die in the Lord, your death is precious in his sight. Christ's promise of the crown of life gives the strength to face imprisonment and death without abandoning the faith.

John sees the great white throne and the one before whose face earth and heaven flee. It is a dreadful judgment. The dead, small and great, stand before God; the books are opened, along with the book of life, and the dead are judged according to their works. The books include the Bible by which the works are judged and the record of those works; the book of life identifies those who receive life.

The sea gives up its dead and death and hell give up theirs. It does not matter whether a person was buried, drowned, burned or had ashes scattered. God can bring every one back. Death and hell are cast into the lake of fire: “This is the second death.” That is the death Christ promises the overcomer will not suffer.

“the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life”. Eternal life is what we want. The elect in the first resurrection have already been judged and do not have to fear the second death. If relatives rejected the truth and died in their sins, their relationship to us does not exempt them from the later judgment.

The rest of the dead do not live again until the thousand years are finished. Blessed and holy is the person who has part in the first resurrection: “on such the second death hath no power”. The first resurrection is when Christ returns for the elect. They have already been judged and are blessed; the remaining dead, including unbelieving relatives, face the later judgment. Do not confuse those two groups or those two times.

sense.text: Christ has the sharp sword with two edges. He addresses the leader of Pergamos and knows where they live, even where Satan's seat is. The city is full of pagan worship and wickedness, yet they hold fast his name and have not denied the faith, even when Antipas, his faithful martyr, was killed among them. Do not be ashamed of the words of the Bible or surrender them because somebody threatens you.

There are still a few things against this church. Some hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to put a stumbling block before Israel: food sacrificed to idols and fornication. Balaam loved the wages of unrighteousness. Covetousness and women became the means of turning Israel from God.

Look at the same spirit in the work today: an artist or video editor demands money and holds the work hostage while another brother completes it quickly for the congregation. Others count how many people are in a school and multiply it by the price of a shirt, thinking of their profit, or want money for multiple wives. Serve the Lord and the people; do not make the work a means of enriching yourself.

The trap can look like advantage: a marriage promises money, property or political standing, but leads away from the commandments. White women were used against black movements in the 1960s. The Undercover Brother example, interracial marriage after Loving v. Virginia, wealthy athletes and the Greenleaf story show the same kind of enticement. In Africa, Chinese men marry women to gain land rights in places such as Uganda, Sierra Leone and Liberia, then leave them and the children. The apparent benefit conceals the stumbling block.

Pergamos also has those holding the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, the worship of Nike, which Christ hates. His command is repent. Otherwise he comes quickly and fights against them with the sword of his mouth. His word brings judgment; belonging to a congregation does not excuse keeping an idolatrous doctrine.

The overcomer receives the hidden manna. Christ is that bread from heaven; it is not merely the physical bread the fathers ate in the wilderness. Receiving his doctrine gives life. The white stone and the new name are further promises to the one who overcomes.

precepts.why: Nineveh is called the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, selling nations through her whoredoms and families through her witchcrafts. Everybody loves that harlot. The same spirit is in America, the mother of harlots: pagan practices and seduction draw whole nations and families in. Pergamos being Satan's seat is about that environment of idolatry and wickedness surrounding the church.

“For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed”. Christ comes in his glory, his Father's glory and that of the holy angels. Do not be ashamed of what the Bible actually says. Holding his name and refusing to deny the faith means standing by his words when they are unpopular or dangerous.

Parents, brethren, kinsfolk and friends will betray believers, and some will be put to death. Some, not all. Even the people closest to you may betray you; we have seen that spirit, including the betrayals in 2018. Antipas was killed, but the church still had to hold the faith. Do not make your loyalty depend on whether relatives or friends remain loyal.

“following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness”. Balaam's problem was covetousness, loving the payment for doing wrong. A brother who makes his service to the congregation conditional on money is walking toward that same trap. God gives gifts for the work, not for holding the people hostage while calculating personal profit.

Israel abode in Shittim and began committing whoredom with the daughters of Moab. That is the stumbling block Balaam's counsel put before the people. The women drew Israel into fornication and the worship connected with it.

Moses asked why the women had been kept alive. “these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor”. A plague came among the congregation because of that trespass. Balaam could not simply curse Israel as Balac wanted, so his counsel used the women to make Israel sin and bring judgment on themselves. Money, political advantage and attractive marriages can still be used to lead men into that same disobedience.

sense.text: Our fathers ate manna in the desert, bread from heaven. Christ explains that Moses did not give the true bread; the Father gives the true bread from heaven, which comes down and gives life to the world. The world here is Israel. The manna in the wilderness was a figure pointing to Christ.

They ask for that bread always, and Christ answers that he is the bread of life. Coming to him and believing in him satisfies hunger and thirst. They had seen him and still did not believe. The hidden manna is Christ and his doctrine, not a promise that ordinary bread will make the flesh immortal.

All whom the Father gives Christ will come to him, and he will not cast out the one who comes. The Father chooses who receives this understanding. Christ came down from heaven to do the will of the one who sent him, not his own will. Follow that obedience instead of making your own will the measure of truth.

The one who believes on Christ has everlasting life. The fathers ate manna and are dead; that physical bread did not prevent death. Christ is the living bread from heaven, and the one who eats it lives for ever. His flesh is given for the life of the world, Israel. Breaking bread points to receiving him and learning his doctrine. That explains the hidden manna promised to the overcomer in Revelation.

precepts.why: “But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. The god of this world has blinded the minds of unbelievers so that the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, the image of God, does not shine to them. White worship blinds our people to Christ and his image. The fact that some can hear the words and still not believe is why Christ calls the manna hidden; the Father has to open the mind to receive it.

sense.text:
The overcomer receives a white stone with a new name written in it, known only to the person who receives it. That new name is the true name, the one you had before the world, not another name for men to argue over now. We do not remember those former things in this life.

John the Baptist did not know that he had been Elijah, but Christ knew. You cannot use your lack of remembrance as proof that there was no former existence. In the kingdom the Lord gives the name he has appointed, and only the recipient knows it. Stop making today's assumed names a quarrel among the people.

precepts.why: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.”. Our spirits were with God before this world was prepared and before we sinned here. Israel agreed to the plan there. The promise of the new name reaches back to who we were before coming into this life.

“There is no remembrance of former things”. Neither will there be remembrance of the things to come among those who come afterward. We do not remember our former lives. John the Baptist not remembering Elijah does not overturn what Christ knew about him. The name given in the kingdom is the true name whose former memory we do not have now.

Zion's righteousness goes forth as brightness and her salvation as a burning lamp. The Gentiles see that righteousness and kings see her glory. “and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.” The Lord names it. Do not waste time arguing over the names people claim today when God has promised the name he himself will give.

The overcomer becomes a pillar in the temple of God, a leader who goes no more out. There is no more captivity. Christ writes on him the name of his God, the name of New Jerusalem coming down from heaven, and his new name. Those names are given in the kingdom. Men disputing over names now need to wait for what Christ has actually promised.

sense.text: The message goes to the leader in Thyatira, a city whose name means daughter. On the map it is close to Ephesus and Pergamos; these congregations lived among the same Greek influences. The Son of God has eyes like a flame of fire and feet like fine brass. He sees the works and the problems of the church.

Christ knows their works, charity, service, faith and patience. Charity is love of your brother and neighbour; service is doing the Lord's work. Their last works are more than the first. This is a working congregation with real good in it, yet it must still correct what follows.

They suffer that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and seduce Christ's servants into fornication and eating things sacrificed to idols. This is not Ahab's wife physically living in the time of Revelation. It is the same spirit appearing again: rebellion, idolatry and a weak man allowing a woman to take control.

Ahab was stirred up by his wife to do wickedness. A wife should help her husband obey God, not use scriptures to argue him into disobedience. The examples of women preaching in churches and a woman taking over street teaching show that same refusal to stay in the order God gave. Revealing clothes and religious authority are being mixed together. Calling oneself spiritual does not give permission to ignore the commandments written by Paul; they are not merely Paul's personal advice.

precepts.why: Lydia was a seller of purple from Thyatira, a woman who worshipped God and heard Paul. The Lord opened her heart so that she attended to what Paul spoke. This locates Thyatira in the apostolic work and shows a woman receiving the teaching in the right order.

“there was none like unto Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.” Ahab's wife stirred him up to wickedness and he allowed it. The Jezebel in Revelation is that same spirit operating through another woman, with men yielding to it. A husband who lets his wife turn him against God's commands is repeating Ahab's failure.

“let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.” If a man thinks himself a prophet or spiritual, this is the test: acknowledge what Paul writes as the Lord's commandments. Do not dismiss the instructions about women or marriage as Paul's opinion whenever they cut against what you want to do.

sense.text:
Demetrius made silver shrines for Diana and brought the craftsmen much gain. Paul was persuading people throughout Ephesus and almost all Asia that gods made with hands were no gods. Demetrius was worried about the loss of their livelihood and the loss of Diana's standing. Religion and money were bound together.

Look at Diana's image, with many breasts: fertility, sexuality and female dominance. The same goddess spirit appears as Astarte and Easter and in the goddess images used by Kemetic worshippers. This is the environment around the churches of Asia Minor. Paul was turning new believers away from a religion that exalted the woman, and the men making money from it fought back.

The craftsmen cried out for Diana, the city filled with confusion, and the crowd seized Gaius and Aristarchus and rushed into the theatre. Paul wanted to enter, but the disciples and friends among the chief men of Asia kept him from doing so. Most of the assembly did not even know why they had gathered. When Alexander was recognized as a Jew, they cried for Diana for about two hours.

That uproar shows how deeply this goddess worship held the city. The doctrine did not disappear from people's minds the moment they heard Paul. The instructions sent to Timothy in Ephesus had to address those former beliefs and restore God's order.

precepts.why: Paul calls Timothy his own son in the faith and reminds him that he was left at Ephesus to charge some that they teach no other doctrine. Ephesus is the city of Diana. Timothy has to keep the congregation from bringing its former goddess religion into the truth. That is the setting for the instruction about women learning in subjection.

sense.text:
A woman is to learn in silence with all subjection. Paul does not suffer a woman to teach or usurp authority over the man. Shut the hell up; do not bring that spirit up in here. He is undoing the order of Diana worship among converts in Ephesus. A woman learning the Bible is right; a woman using it to take authority over the man is the problem.

America has gathered the evil of the former captivities together. Even entertainment keeps promoting the reversal, with female action heroes and Wonder Woman shown as the ruling power. Do not bring that pattern into the congregation and call it righteousness.

Adam was formed first, then Eve. Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and was in the transgression. Paul gives the reason from the beginning; it is not simply a local custom with no spiritual basis. The order of creation and the fall explain why the woman must not usurp the man.

Being saved in childbearing does not mean every woman who has a child is automatically saved. The conditions follow: continue in faith, charity, holiness and sobriety. Sobriety is wisdom and a sound mind. The pain of childbirth recalls Eve's transgression and the order God pronounced afterward. A woman must keep the faith and God's order, not merely give birth.

precepts.why: God multiplied the woman's sorrow and conception and appointed sorrow in bringing forth children. “and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Childbearing is tied to what happened with Eve, who took the lead in disobedience. The pain reminds the woman of that transgression. The husband's rule is God's order, while salvation still requires the faith, charity, holiness and sobriety Paul named.

sense.text: Christ gave her space to repent of her fornication, and she did not repent. The problem is not that no correction or opportunity was given; she refuses it. Rebellion is witchcraft and stubbornness is idolatry. When a woman exalts her own words above God's, that is the spirit being corrected.

Christ casts her into a bed and those committing adultery with her into great tribulation unless they repent. He kills her children with death. The children are her followers, the people adopting and defending her doctrine, not a command to attack literal babies. All the churches will know that Christ searches the reins and hearts and gives each person according to his works. Men following and protecting the rebellion are accountable too.

There are others in Thyatira who do not hold this doctrine and have not known the depths of Satan. There are levels to that wickedness: yielding to a rebellious woman, money, your own lusts and white worship. Christ puts no other burden on those who have kept away from it.

A mother can counsel her son to do wickedly. A husband can listen to his wife against God's command, as Adam did. Do not let loyalty to a mother or wife become permission to disobey God. Some men allow a woman to hit them, dominate them or use sex to control them, then defend her against every correction. Captains cannot teach one thing before the congregation and let the opposite rule their own homes.

The correction is to repent and fix the church. Christ does not tell everybody to leave the congregation because it has a problem. Address the sin, allow repentance and restore the right order.

This is not hatred of women or an instruction for women to remain ignorant. Righteous sisters learn the scriptures, help their husbands, raise their children and teach younger women. Their abilities are valuable in the place God appointed. What must stop is turning that ability into authority over the man. A woman pushing a doctrine that Israel is only black people can influence her husband into excluding the northern kingdom; holding a Bible does not make that doctrine right. Deborah was subject to the governors and was married; Barak was not her husband. His weakness led to the honour going to a woman. Do not turn that history into permission to reverse God's order.

“But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” Hold the understanding and the scriptures already given. The sixty-six books with the Apocrypha, eighty books, are enough to hold until Christ comes. Stop chasing other books as though God has left you without what you need.

The one who overcomes and keeps Christ's works to the end receives power over the nations. His works are God's law, covenants, statutes and commandments. The end is Christ's return or the end of your life; keep doing the work until then. The kingdom is not equality among the nations. Israel is given power to rule them.

The rod of iron is rule that enforces God's law. The nations are broken like a potter's vessels. They will obey the Bible, including its dietary laws, and their true national identities will be restored: China as Moab, Japan as Ammon and the Palestinians as Philistines. This is the authority the Father promised Christ, and Christ shares it with those who overcome.

The power to take the kingdom belongs to that future fulfillment. Not now. Do not turn a prophecy of what the Lord will do then into an excuse for some crazy brother to act now. The Lord appears over his people, gives them power and brings the promised rule.

The morning star is Christ. He gives greater wisdom and understanding, making the overcomers like him. Whoever has an ear must hear what the Spirit says to the churches. These promises and corrections require understanding and obedience.

precepts.why: “For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” That is why refusing to repent is more than a personality problem. A woman who insists on her own authority against God's command is practicing the same rebellion and idolatry as Jezebel, even if she calls herself a prophetess.

The men knew their wives were burning incense to other gods, and the women stood in a great multitude with the people dwelling in Egypt, in Pathros. They answered Jeremiah that they would not hearken to the word spoken in the Lord's name. Instead they would do whatever went out of their own mouth and burn incense to the queen of heaven.

That is open rebellion: our own mouth over God's word. The queen of heaven is the same goddess spirit seen in Isis and Diana. The women insist on it and the men allow it. This explains the Jezebel doctrine that the church has been tolerating.

“set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them”. God commands the man to oppose women inventing prophecy out of their own hearts. Do not excuse a false doctrine because the woman is your wife. The correction has to be spoken.

Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds to bring Athaliah out within the ranges and kill the man following her. The men enforcing the priest's command did not submit to the woman or protect the men supporting her rebellion. Her followers shared the judgment. That explains why Christ threatens both Jezebel and her children, the adherents of her doctrine.

“for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.” A mother can counsel her son into the ways of Ahab's house. Being your mother does not make her counsel God's counsel. Mama's boys who follow her against the commandments repeat that evil.

“Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife”. Adam knew what God commanded, but listened to his wife instead. That choice is the problem. A husband must not make his wife's wishes greater than God's word, even when she pressures him or makes obedience difficult. The same test can come through another man; no person's counsel replaces God's command.

“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands”. Her heart traps the man and her hands bind him, preventing him from doing God's work. “whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”. Escape comes through pleasing God, not catering to the rebellion.

This is the Jezebel spirit in a home or congregation. Men in leadership cannot keep excusing it while professing to teach the opposite. The instruction is to correct the sin and repent, not abandon the church whenever a problem appears. Righteous sisters receive their place as helpers and teachers of children and younger women; the snare is the woman making herself a goddess over the man.

Moses asks the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, to “set a man over the congregation”. That man goes out and comes in before them, leads them out and brings them in, so they are not sheep without a shepherd. The leader, including the one leading them to war, is a man. This is the order the goddess religions try to reverse.

“But his law have they despised, and denied his covenants; in his statutes have they not been faithful, and have not performed his works.” His works are bound to his law, covenants and statutes. Keeping Christ's works to the end means remaining faithful in these things, not inventing a religion in which obedience no longer matters.

The Lord defends Jerusalem; the feeble among them are as David, and the house of David is as God, as the angel of the Lord before them. The house of David is the 144,000. They receive spiritual power to carry out the promised rule. Even the feeble are made strong; this authority does not come from the strength we have now.

“But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom”. Take the kingdom, not ask the nations to give it to us. The saints receive the power promised by Christ. That is a future act under the Lord, not permission to go out and do something now.

Turn to the strong hold, prisoners of hope. We are prisoners in America with hope in God, and the Bible is our strong hold. The Lord promises double, bends Judah as his bow and fills it with Ephraim, raising Zion against Greece and making his people like the sword of a mighty man.

The Lord is seen over them; his arrow goes forth as lightning, he blows the trumpet and goes with the whirlwinds of the south. He appears above his people with the angels and chariots. That is when the power to take the kingdom is given. It is not now; do not mistake the future judgment for a present command to act.

God sets his king on the holy hill of Zion and declares him his Son. He tells him to ask for the heathen as his inheritance and the uttermost parts of the earth as his possession. “Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” The Father promised Christ that rule over the whole earth. Revelation repeats the promise as Christ gives a share in it to the overcomers.

“And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. The faithful Israelites of the first resurrection inherit with Christ. What the Father promised him in Psalms 2, he shares with them in Revelation 2: power over the nations and the rod of iron. The inheritance is why Christ can promise them what he received of his Father.
